2-1.title: Vector Spear
2-1.setup: Spearhead Wing enters a formation grid where enemy screens close every open lane.
2-1.wing: Break the lead pair first; the rest of the lattice will lose its timing.
2-1.result: The grid collapses and the relief convoy reaches the fleet yards.
2-1.consequence: Command authorizes specialist hull trials for the next sortie.

2-2.title: The Empty Wing
2-2.setup: A disabled defense wing leaves one corridor open and every other route under crossfire.
2-2.wing: Choose the hull that covers the missing role; this fight punishes a copied loadout.
2-2.result: The squad fills the gap long enough to recover the stranded pilots.
2-2.consequence: Recovered telemetry unlocks the first Spearhead equipment component.

2-3.title: Lockstorm
2-3.setup: Missile carriers seed the lane with overlapping locks while scouts screen their launchers.
2-3.wing: Use the warning rhythm, cut across one lock at a time, and do not drag the pattern into the convoy.
2-3.result: The carriers lose their targeting net and retreat behind the fleet yards.
2-3.consequence: The enemy begins rotating formations to deny the same counter twice.

2-4.title: Tempered Hull
2-4.setup: Armor foundries turn unfinished warships into a moving wall around the assembly ring.
2-4.wing: Strip the escorts, then strike the foundry vents before the next hull seals.
2-4.result: The assembly ring survives and its engineers finish a countermeasure package.
2-4.consequence: Specialist crews can now trade raw damage for formation control.

2-5.title: Rook's Intercept
2-5.setup: A pursuit group slips past the main line and marks the medical transports.
2-5.wing: I will catch the locks; stay on my vector and erase anything that turns toward the transports.
2-5.result: Rook intercepts the final salvo with seconds to spare.
2-5.consequence: The rescued crews volunteer targeting data for the rotating-grid assault.

2-6.title: Wheel of Fire
2-6.setup: The enemy rotates five attack wings around a protected command spindle.
2-6.wing: The wheel changes direction after every break; watch the leader, not the nearest target.
2-6.result: The spindle falls and the wheel fragments into isolated flights.
2-6.consequence: A defense-set core is recovered from the command spindle.

2-7.title: Chaff Window
2-7.setup: Countermeasure clouds hide mines and split friendly lock indicators from real threats.
2-7.wing: Fire only inside the clean window; false locks are meant to empty our heavy magazines.
2-7.result: The squad crosses the chaff belt without losing a ship.
2-7.consequence: Command maps a specialist route through the fleet-yard perimeter.

2-8.title: Split Vector
2-8.setup: Two supply lanes diverge around an active fabrication yard and both call for help.
2-8.wing: The fast lane saves fuel cells; the hard lane saves the crews who know how to use them.
2-8.result: The chosen lane is secured and the other force adapts to the squad's absence.
2-8.consequence: The operation records which specialist role the fleet values under pressure.

2-9.title: Five-Ship Oath
2-9.setup: Every surviving specialist wing joins one synchronized strike against the yard shield.
2-9.wing: One missed beat resets the shield. Hold your fire until all five markers align.
2-9.result: The shield drops in a single coordinated volley.
2-9.consequence: The final Spearhead set component and a path to doctrine command are recovered.

2-10.title: Spearhead Crown
2-10.setup: Doctrine Command locks the fleet yards into a rotating fortress of specialist counters.
2-10.wing: It knows every role separately; make it answer combinations it was never trained to read.
2-10.result: Doctrine Command is defeated and the formation war ends.
2-10.consequence: The fleet must choose whether future specialist wings operate independently or as one formation.

3-1.title: Glass Salvage
3-1.setup: The squad enters a violet ruin field where intact alien capacitors drift among brittle wreckage.
3-1.wing: Salvage only the blue cores; the clear shells are pressure traps.
3-1.result: A stable capacitor reaches the research deck without rupturing.
3-1.consequence: Alien energy can now be redirected instead of merely avoided.

variants.independent: Independent wings scout separate ruin lanes and return with competing solutions.
variants.unified: The unified specialist formation holds one safe corridor through the ruins.

3-2.title: Borrowed Fire
3-2.setup: Converted alien rounds can be reflected through a shield lattice guarding the archive approach.
3-2.wing: Catch the slow violet shots and return them through the matching emitters.
3-2.result: The squad opens the lattice using the enemy's own charge.
3-2.consequence: Conversion techniques spread to every active wing.

3-3.title: The Drift
3-3.setup: An anomaly bends movement vectors while dormant machines wake along the safe line.
3-3.wing: Trust the projected lane, not the stars; the whole field is sliding sideways.
3-3.result: The squad crosses before the drift closes around the rear guard.
3-3.consequence: Navigation finds coordinates that do not appear on normal charts.

3-4.title: Quiet Coordinates
3-4.setup: A hidden beacon transmits from inside a machine graveyard that reacts to weapon fire.
3-4.wing: Keep the chain controlled. A loud victory here would wake the entire graveyard.
3-4.result: The beacon is recovered with the largest machines still dormant.
3-4.consequence: Its coordinates reveal a secret route beneath the Veil.

3-5.title: Phase Scar
3-5.setup: Rift pulses move hazards between planes and expose targets for only a few seconds.
3-5.wing: Mark the pulse cadence; a target you chase now may return behind you.
3-5.result: The squad seals the widest scar and stabilizes the approach.
3-5.consequence: The archive begins translating the machines' phase commands.

3-6.title: Point of No Return
3-6.setup: The fleet must commit through one of two phase channels before both collapse.
3-6.wing: The bright channel is faster; the dark channel reaches the missing survey team.
3-6.result: The chosen channel holds long enough for the committed force to pass.
3-6.consequence: The abandoned channel becomes an enemy reinforcement route.

3-7.title: Conversion Cascade
3-7.setup: Linked emitters multiply every reflected projectile until the arena fills with borrowed fire.
3-7.wing: Break the links from outside in, or one mistake will feed the whole cascade.
3-7.result: The cascade is turned against its anchor and burns itself out.
3-7.consequence: The archive unlocks a map of the Veil's central breach.

3-8.title: Archive in the Storm
3-8.setup: The complete alien archive hangs inside an unstable ion storm guarded by phase sentinels.
3-8.wing: We can extract it, but we must decide who is allowed to use what it remembers.
3-8.result: The archive is recovered and the storm collapses behind the squad.
3-8.consequence: Command asks whether the archive should be shared with the fleet or sealed.

3-9.title: Veil Breach
3-9.setup: The machines open a breach large enough to move an invasion wing through the ruins.
3-9.wing: Cut the anchor pairs before the center opens; there will be no room to dodge afterward.
3-9.result: The breach is narrowed to a single command channel.
3-9.consequence: The archive decision changes which allies arrive for the final assault.

variants.shared: Allied analysts use the shared archive to expose the breach anchors on every display.
variants.sealed: Kael's sealed archive team guides the squad alone through an unmarked service channel.

3-10.title: The Shattered Gate
3-10.setup: Veil Command combines phase jumps, conversion fields, and machine guardians at the central gate.
3-10.wing: Every trick in this theater is active at once. Read the color, then the cadence, then the safe plane.
3-10.result: The gate shatters and the ancient machines fall silent.
3-10.consequence: Fragments of the Veil point toward a three-faction war already in progress.

4-1.title: Flags in the Static
4-1.setup: Human, raider, and alien formations collide around a civilian signal lost in weapons static.
4-1.wing: Identify silhouettes before firing; a neutral loss will turn this rescue into another front.
4-1.result: The civilians escape while all three fleets reassess the squad.
4-1.consequence: Every later objective now carries a faction cost.

4-2.title: Who Comes First
4-2.setup: Two damaged formations request protection while an orbital battery acquires both.
4-2.wing: We cannot cover every marker. Choose the objective whose loss the front cannot absorb.
4-2.result: The selected formation survives and the other withdraws under fire.
4-2.consequence: Faction commanders begin pricing cooperation against the squad's priorities.

4-3.title: Wounded Systems
4-3.setup: Ion shrapnel disables engines, weapons, and shields in alternating sectors.
4-3.wing: Do not spend the system you need next; the disable cycle is visible on the outer ring.
4-3.result: The squad reaches a repair dock with all critical systems recoverable.
4-3.consequence: Engineers adapt the shield to survive the orbital-weapon corridor.

4-4.title: Hammer Above
4-4.setup: An orbital weapon sweeps the contested system while ground batteries feed it targeting solutions.
4-4.wing: Hide in its shadow, destroy one uplink per pass, and never cross the gold warning line late.
4-4.result: The Hammer loses its surface lock and fires blind into empty space.
4-4.consequence: Its control codes become a weapon the squad can capture.

4-5.title: The Corridor
4-5.setup: A narrow evacuation corridor can protect either civilians or the defense fleet's damaged carriers.
4-5.wing: Whichever group enters first will own the safe timing for the rest of the operation.
4-5.result: The chosen group clears the corridor before the orbital battery reacquires.
4-5.consequence: The unchosen faction remembers the delay and changes its support.

4-6.title: Three Fires
4-6.setup: Three objectives fail on different clocks while mixed fleets attack one another inside the defense zone.
4-6.wing: Stabilize the shortest clock, then pivot. Chasing the loudest fight loses all three.
4-6.result: The squad preserves the objective chain and prevents a general rout.
4-6.consequence: A defense-set core is assembled from all three factions' technology.

variants.civilians: Civilian pilots reveal hidden repair caches along the defense route.
variants.fleet: Defense carriers extend a shield screen across the first objective zone.

4-7.title: Repair Window
4-7.setup: A mobile repair tender must cross open space between synchronized orbital strikes.
4-7.wing: Defend the tender, not the enemies. The next repair window closes in twenty seconds.
4-7.result: The tender restores the surviving carriers before the final strike.
4-7.consequence: The repaired fleet offers cover for the weapon-capture attempt.

4-8.title: Stolen Sun
4-8.setup: Raiders seize the orbital weapon and turn its reactor beam on every faction.
4-8.wing: Capture the control nodes intact; destroying them only leaves the beam firing.
4-8.result: The squad redirects the weapon into an empty debris belt.
4-8.consequence: Control of the Hammer breaks the stalemate and exposes the three command ships.

4-9.title: No Neutral Sky
4-9.setup: The three fleets converge, and every target changes allegiance as command ships issue new orders.
4-9.wing: Track behavior and markings together. Color alone is no longer enough.
4-9.result: The squad forces a ceasefire corridor through the center of the battle.
4-9.consequence: All command ships accept one final engagement to settle the front.

4-10.title: War of Three Banners
4-10.setup: Three command ships fight for the orbital crown while the Hammer cycles beneath them.
4-10.wing: Disable each banner's weapon before finishing its command core, or the others inherit the gun.
4-10.result: The crown is neutralized and the three-faction war ends without an orbital massacre.
4-10.consequence: The surviving coalition points the squad toward the Last Arsenal.

5-1.title: Red Screen
5-1.setup: An elite screen tests the fleet with perfect spacing and weapons tuned to punish common builds.
5-1.wing: They expect the standard answer. Change range and damage type before they finish measuring us.
5-1.result: The screen breaks formation for the first time in its service record.
5-1.consequence: The Arsenal begins deploying archived war machines.

5-2.title: Old Debts
5-2.setup: A rebuilt miniboss returns with armor covering the part the squad destroyed in the first campaign.
5-2.wing: The old weakness is bait. Watch which system powers the new plate.
5-2.result: The returning machine is defeated by a new counter rather than a repeated script.
5-2.consequence: Its core identifies the Arsenal's adaptive foundry.

5-3.title: Measure of the Build
5-3.setup: Three locked arenas test burst damage, survival, and control in rapid succession.
5-3.wing: No build wins every room the same way; spend resources where your hull is weakest.
5-3.result: The squad clears all three checks without abandoning its chosen identity.
5-3.consequence: Command approves endgame upgrade limits from the combat data.

5-4.title: Legendary Weight
5-4.setup: A high-tier equipment vault is attached to a carrier that sheds armor as it accelerates.
5-4.wing: The vault is optional, but taking it means fighting the carrier at full speed.
5-4.result: The carrier falls and the vault survives the extraction.
5-4.consequence: The recovered component opens a costly but distinct build path.

5-5.title: Consequence Fleet
5-5.setup: The Arsenal fields ships rebuilt from factions and technologies shaped by earlier decisions.
5-5.wing: These are consequences with engines. Identify which campaign choice produced each counter.
5-5.result: The squad defeats the fleet without erasing the allies still trapped inside it.
5-5.consequence: Recovered crews reveal the route to the adaptive foundry.

5-6.title: The Long Gauntlet
5-6.setup: Six elite gates run without a full recovery interval and every gate changes the safe range.
5-6.wing: Bank resources before the fourth gate. The first three are designed to make you feel rich.
5-6.result: The squad exits the gauntlet with the formation intact.
5-6.consequence: A mastery core is forged from the six defeated elite systems.

5-7.title: Counterfeit Victory
5-7.setup: The Arsenal deploys weakened variants that explode into their true patterns when finished too quickly.
5-7.wing: A fast kill is not always a clean kill. Read the core before committing the chain.
5-7.result: The squad dismantles the false victories without triggering a cascade.
5-7.consequence: The foundry loses its supply of copied command cores.

5-8.title: Arsenal Mastery
5-8.setup: The adaptive foundry mirrors the squad's equipped weapon, spell, and defense priorities.
5-8.wing: It can copy numbers, not judgment. Force its mirrored systems into the wrong range.
5-8.result: The foundry overloads while trying to maintain incompatible copied builds.
5-8.consequence: The Arsenal's final siege line loses the ability to adapt.

5-9.title: The Last Arsenal
5-9.setup: Every surviving war machine defends the sealed command foundry in layered siege rings.
5-9.wing: This is a campaign of counters compressed into one approach. Keep the restart loop short and deliberate.
5-9.result: The siege rings fall and the command foundry is exposed.
5-9.consequence: The final Arsenal set component is recovered before the command decision.

5-10.title: Ashes or Ammunition
5-10.setup: Arsenal Command activates every stored pattern and threatens to launch the foundry into the home fleet.
5-10.wing: Break the launch clamps between phases; winning the duel means nothing if the foundry escapes.
5-10.result: Arsenal Command falls and the launch is stopped.
5-10.consequence: The fleet must dismantle the foundry or turn it against the final invasion.

6-1.title: All Fronts
6-1.setup: The invasion reaches every defended lane at once and no reserve remains outside the squad.
6-1.wing: We cannot be everywhere, but we can keep one route open long enough for the fleets to converge.
6-1.result: The first invasion line breaks and the homeward route remains open.
6-1.consequence: The Arsenal decision determines what firepower joins the defense.

variants.dismantled: Components from the dismantled Arsenal reinforce every allied shield on the route.
variants.deployed: The deployed Arsenal burns a narrow attack corridor through the invasion line.

6-2.title: Braided Assault
6-2.setup: Human, raider, alien, and elite formations braid their attacks around one shared command pulse.
6-2.wing: Separate the pulse leaders; the mixed formations are strongest only while they share a beat.
6-2.result: The braid unravels into four readable attack groups.
6-2.consequence: Allied wings learn to combine without inheriting the invasion's command weakness.

6-3.title: Rift Weather
6-3.setup: Anomalies, ion storms, debris, and missile fronts overlap above the homeworld approach.
6-3.wing: Treat the environment as a moving formation. Safe space travels clockwise after every pulse.
6-3.result: The fleet crosses the rift weather with its evacuation lanes intact.
6-3.consequence: A stable route to the invasion core appears for ninety minutes.

6-4.title: Hold Everything
6-4.setup: Rescue, escort, sabotage, and defense objectives activate across one collapsing station.
6-4.wing: Complete the objective in front of you before chasing the next alarm; partial rescues save no one.
6-4.result: The station holds and every completed objective feeds the final fleet.
6-4.consequence: The defense gains one last repair and resupply point.

6-5.title: Fleet's Answer
6-5.setup: Command asks the assembled fleets to commit to one approach before the invasion core closes.
6-5.wing: The answer changes who leads, who screens, and which route remains available after us.
6-5.result: The chosen fleet plan launches without a split command.
6-5.consequence: Earlier alliances visibly determine the ships present in the next battle.

6-6.title: Commanders' Fall
6-6.setup: Major command ships from every operation guard the invasion core in a linked boss sequence.
6-6.wing: Each commander keeps its own rule. Reset your assumptions when the arena changes.
6-6.result: The command sequence ends and the core loses its outer authority layer.
6-6.consequence: Only the allied consequences and the central invasion mind remain.

6-7.title: What We Saved
6-7.setup: Allies preserved by earlier routes and objectives arrive while abandoned assets return as enemy variants.
6-7.wing: Protect the people who made it here; they are not background decoration for our final score.
6-7.result: The allied formation survives and opens the homeworld corridor.
6-7.consequence: Every major campaign choice now contributes a visible final-battle modifier.

6-8.title: Homeward Vector
6-8.setup: The squad races the invasion core toward the homeworld defense ring through a narrowing approach.
6-8.wing: Use the expert route if you can hold the chain; the safe route preserves more allied ships.
6-8.result: The squad reaches the defense ring before the core can anchor.
6-8.consequence: The invasion has one remaining opportunity to force a final decision.

6-9.title: One Last Order
6-9.setup: The invasion offers a false ceasefire while charging the weapon beneath its command shell.
6-9.wing: The words are a timer. Break the charge relays before answering with weapons.
6-9.result: The false ceasefire fails and the command shell opens.
6-9.consequence: The fleet enters Convergence with no unresolved tactical objective.

6-10.title: Convergence
6-10.setup: The invasion mind combines every campaign mechanic around the homeworld and its surviving fleets.
6-10.wing: Read one layer at a time: formation, hazard, objective, commander, then core.
6-10.result: The invasion mind is defeated and the homeworld remains free.
6-10.consequence: Victory leaves one final choice: rebuild the frontier or guard the Convergence forever.
